class_guess: Bell eats counter: BECv1 tm10 with a broken carry (spaced-digit binary counter + unary marker)
summary: BECv1 tm10 twin (E1 differs): spaced-digit counter eats a unary run; 7 rules validated, EatDigit open
mechanism: Tape: a counter on the left, then a long run of 110 blocks holding a 2-cell 00 marker.
Each round: A sweeps right to the marker, moves it 1 block left, B sweeps back, counter +1 (same as BECv1 tm10).
Unlike tm10 (E1), digits are 111110 blocks spread through the 110 run; the marker eats the lowest digit on arrival.

template.note:
Simulated our TM on tm10's cert: 10/11 hypotheses hold (HR1-3, HE0-3, HL1,3,4,5; 25/25 each); HL2 = binary carry 1<E1 -> <E11 fails 0/25.
So the unary half carries over verbatim; LeftBinaryCounter must become a spaced-digit counter (5-blocks + 110 filler).

strategy:
Keep BECv1's unary half (HR1-3, HE0-3 as es-lemmas). Replace LeftBinaryCounter by an Inductive digit list (5-digit + filler gaps, 4-mode at the MSB), BECv7.v style;
prove OP/OQ by ind over sweeps + carries, then a finite EatDigit case table; close with progress_nonhalt_cond on a shape predicate (any gaps G,M), as BECv7's canonical.
risks: EatDigit is messy: it makes 3/4/6 blocks and a transient second 00 marker; the case table may be large.
Digit gaps evolve irregularly (3,7 -> 10 -> 17 -> 11 ...): proof must quantify over all gaps (shape invariant), not track values.
